summary.headline: Nitin Spinners Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR859.8 crore (+7.4% QoQ) and EBITDA margin rose to 15.17%, with management guiding to a 16-20% normalised margin in FY27.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR859.8 crore, up 7.4% QoQ and 2.2% YoY, driven by better demand and yarn prices. EBITDA rose 16.9% QoQ to INR130.4 crore, with margin up 124 bps QoQ to 15.17%, and PAT reached INR57.4 crore. For full FY26, revenue fell 2.8% to INR3,213.9 crore and EBITDA fell 4% to INR452.8 crore, while PAT rose 1.2% to INR177.6 crore. Management said the capex programme (fabric and spinning expansion, renewable power) is on track for H2 FY27 commissioning.

segments.name: Yarn
segments.commentary: Yarn was 74% of FY26 revenue; spinning capacity ran at over 98% utilisation in Q4 FY26, with management guiding 97-98% going forward. Average yarn spread (realisation over cotton cost, around 33-34 count) is about INR120-125/kg, up from about INR110/kg last quarter.

segments.name: Fabric (woven and knitted)
segments.commentary: Fabric was 21% of FY26 revenue (woven about 18%, knitted about 4%, per the Q&A corrections). Woven capacity ran at over 90% utilisation in Q4; woven realisation rose about 2-2.5% QoQ and knitted about 5% QoQ. Knitted utilisation is below normal, with a 65-70% normal level expected to return in 1-1.5 years.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Exports were about 63% of Q4 FY26 revenue (61.9% for FY26); domestic was 37% in Q4 (31.8% for FY26).

guidance_outlook: Normalised EBITDA margin range of 16-20%, which management expects to reach in FY27.

Fabric capex adds 35 million metres, taking capacity to 75 million metres (errata to 70 million metres as stated), and spinning adds 22,000 tonnes to about 130,000 tonnes. Commissioning in H2 FY27: fabric from October-December 2026 and spinning from January-February 2027.

Capex of about INR1,000-1,100 crore is expected to add more than INR1,000 crore to top line. Normalisation of yarn prices may add 5-7% to existing turnover. Management expects 30-35% revenue growth on the existing base over time.

Renewable power: about 75 MW added including PPAs, reaching close to 100 MW installed. A 10 MW hybrid PPA is due by Q3 FY27. Expected savings of INR50 crore per year at full run-rate, with INR30-35 crore in the current year.
Total debt expected at INR1,900-2,000 crore after commissioning, including working capital. Average borrowing cost about 5.6%, working capital under 7%, blended about 6.5%.
Asset turn of about 1.2-1.3x at company level; new capex expected at about 1:1 excluding renewable capex.
capex_capacity: Fabric capacity expansion adds 35 million metres (to about 75 million metres, errata). Spinning adds 22,000 tonnes (to about 130,000 tonnes). Commissioning in H2 FY27.

Over INR300 crore spent so far, including about INR140 crore in capital advances, about INR55-60 crore capitalised from modernisation and balancing, and capital WIP of about INR100 crore. The balance is to be funded by internal accruals and debt.
Additional energy capex of about INR230-240 crore, not planned before last year. Renewable power capex is on schedule for H2 FY27.

Rajasthan Investment Promotion Scheme incentives include capital subsidy (about 20-27% of eligible investment, paid over 10 years), interest subsidy (5% of term loan or 2.5% of eligible fixed investment, whichever is lower, for 5 years), plus electricity duty and mandi tax rebates. Management did not quantify the total.
demand_pricing: Demand improved in Q4 FY26 in both domestic and export markets, driven by US tariff removal, downstream restocking and longer transit times. Management said exports of about 100 million kg of yarn a year are steady, with a possible 5-10% increase.

Yarn spread (realisation over cotton) rose to about INR120-125/kg from about INR110/kg last quarter. Management called INR120-125 the median and said it should be sustainable, with a minimum of INR100/kg against an earlier floor of INR90/kg.
Polyester prices rose more than 20% after the West Asia conflict, but synthetic yarn spreads stayed flat. Blended yarn margins improved marginally.

Cotton: domestic prices were INR52,000-55,000 per candy in the lowest period, around 4 years low, and have been rising since recent weeks. Duty on imported cotton was removed Aug-Dec 2025; the industry is asking for a repeat removal.
Fabric prices lag yarn: the company has already raised fabric prices, and management expects further improvement. The India-UK and India-EU FTAs are expected to add European and UK orders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised yarn spread and margin, excluding inventory gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the spread was about INR90/kg at the low end historically and about INR140-150/kg at the high end; a minimum of INR100/kg is now the floor, and INR120-125/kg is sustainable. Last year's margin at INR110 was about 11.5-12%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the freight and gas cost impacts from the war?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe sea freight is up 75-80% and other regions 15-20% versus February, but freight is normally passed on under FOB terms and has normalised since March. Gas-based yarn is a very small share, with under a day of disruption and gas costs up about 1.7x since February.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the duty removal on cotton and the top-line outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the duty removal is up to the government, with a possible permanent fix in 5-6 months. Top-line growth is expected from the INR1,000 crore+ capex, yarn normalisation (5-7%) and recovery, for 30-35% growth on the existing base.

qa_highlights.question: What are the fabric and knitted utilisation trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Knitted utilisation is expected to recover to the normal 65-70% within 1-1.5 years, as US tariffs were reduced from 50%. Some customers were lost to competing countries and are being regained.

risks_watch: Cotton import duty status and cotton availability. The industry wants duty removed; government has not committed to a timeline.
West Asia conflict: transit times up about 2 weeks, sea freight volatile, and polyester and gas costs rising. Management says these are passed on, but synthetic spreads have not widened.
Capex execution: commissioning slips from H2 FY27, and ramp-up of new fabric and yarn capacity. Management said it can increase the reach of fabric to European and UK buyers under the FTAs.
Knitted fabric utilisation is well below normal, at the 65-70% benchmark, and customers were lost in the US tariff period.
Future capex plans are not yet quantified. Management declined to give future capex or fabric margin targets.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the near-term outlook, with management pointing to a record quarter, a 124 bps margin gain and firm yarn spreads. Cautious where the questions turned to the war, cotton duty and timing of FTAs, and it declined to give timelines for government action or future capex.
key_quotes: This is our highest ever quarterly revenue, driven by improvement in demand and yarn prices.
As regards to the present ongoing capex, the plan is progressing very well. It is expected to commercialize in second half of FY '27.
So instead of per unit capex, we need to look at what is the total saving which we can generate out of this.
